highlights:
# Authentication

Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.

The MrScraper API uses API token authentication to secure all endpoints. Every request must include a valid API token in the HTTP request headers.

## Getting Your API Token

API tokens are managed directly from your MrScraper dashboard.

Sign in to your MrScraper Dashboard.

Click your profile icon in the top-right corner and select API Tokens (or go to app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens).

Click New Token.

Enter a descriptive token name and choose an expiration date.

Click Create, then copy and securely store the generated token.

Keep Your Token Secure

Your API token grants access to your account and plan resources. Never expose your token in client-side code (like browsers or mobile apps), and store it securely in an environment variable or server configuration.

## Authenticating Requests

Include your API token in the `x-api-token` HTTP header on every request:

Copy Text

```
x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```

### Marketplace Endpoints

For Marketplace endpoints, authenticate using the standard RFC 6750 `Authorization` header with a Bearer token:

Copy Text

```
Authorization: Bearer <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```

## Verify Token

To test your authentication and confirm that your token is valid, make a request to the `/subscription-accounts` endpoint:

Copy Text

```
curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts" \
  -H "accept: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
```

## Analytics Authentication

Analytics endpoints authenticate using the same `x-api-token` header as all other API endpoints.

When querying analytics, you can also pass the `apiTokenName` query parameter to filter status data for a specific token by the name you assigned when creating it:

Copy Text

```
curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/analytic/statuses?domain=example.com&startDate=2026-04-12%2000:00:00&endDate=2026-04-13%2023:59:59&apiTokenName=YOUR_TOKEN_NAME" \
  -H "accept: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
```

Note

The `apiTokenName` query parameter filters metrics by the token's name (e.g., `production-worker`).

highlights:
# MCP Server

Official MrScraper MCP server for retrieving web pages, web search, and account usage. Connect AI clients or run the open-source server locally.

MrScraper MCP is the official Model Context Protocol server for MrScraper. It connects AI clients to web page retrieval, web search, and your account usage.

...

Package information

This page documents `@mrscraper/mcp` version 0.5.0. Its seven tools share their descriptions, inputs, and defaults with the MrScraper CLI, SDKs, and integrations. 0.5.0 replaced `scraperAPI` with `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, and `getScreenshot`, added `scrapeBrand` and `scrapeJson`, renamed the inputs to camel case, and changed the OAuth scopes. See Migration from the previous tool set.

...

## Requirements

- A MrScraper account
- An MCP client with Streamable HTTP support
- An API key only when the client cannot use OAuth 2.1 or when running the server locally

## Quick start with the hosted server

Add the hosted endpoint

Configure a Streamable HTTP server named `mrscraper` with no credential:

Copy Text

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Use this exact URL, including the `/mcp` path.

Sign in

Connect or reload the MCP server. Your client follows the OAuth 2.1 challenge, opens MrScraper in your browser, and asks you to approve `scrape:read` for the six scraping and search tools and `account:read` for `status`.

Reload and verify

Reload the client or start a new session, then inspect its MCP tool list. The connection should expose `status`, `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, `getScreenshot`, `scrapeBrand`, `scrapeJson`, and `webSearch`.

## Copyable AI setup prompt

Copy Text

```
Connect MrScraper MCP to this agent. Detect the current MCP client and use its native Streamable HTTP setup to add a server named mrscraper at exactly https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp with no static credential. Complete the OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in; if it does not start automatically, use the client's MCP login or authenticate command. Only if the client does not support OAuth, fall back to a MrScraper API key from https://app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens stored through the client's environment-variable or secret-storage mechanism and sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>. Reload the MCP client when required, then list the tools and confirm that status, scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, getScreenshot, scrapeBrand, scrapeJson, and webSearch are available.
```

...

### Other MCP clients

Use these connection values:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Name | `mrscraper` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| URL | `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` |
| Authentication | OAuth 2.1; do not configure a static header |

## API key fallback

If a client cannot complete OAuth, create an API key, store it through the client's secret mechanism, and send it as a bearer token:

Copy Text

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

For Codex, pass the environment-variable name instead of embedding the key:

Copy Text

```
export MRSCRAPER_API_KEY="YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
codex mcp add mrscraper \
  --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var MRSCRAPER_API_KEY
```

## Authentication

| Connection | Credential source |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted Streamable HTTP | OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in, or an API key fallback |
| Self-hosted Streamable HTTP | OAuth 2.1 access token, or `Authorization: Bearer <MrScraper API key>` |
| Local stdio | `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY`, then `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` |

The hosted server publishes OAuth 2.1 protected-resource metadata and challenges unauthenticated clients to start browser sign-in. Access tokens are issued for the exact `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` resource. A tool called without its required scope returns `403 insufficient_scope`, and your client can offer to grant the missing permission.

| Scope | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| `scrape:read` | `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, `getScreenshot`, `scrapeBrand`, `scrapeJson`, and `webSearch` |
| `account:read` | `status` |

These are the only application scopes the server advertises; the authorization server also offers `offline_access` for refresh tokens. Clients take the scopes from the server's metadata, so don't pin scopes in client configurations.

OAuth connections that already hold `scrape:read` keep working without reconnecting; `scrape:write` is no longer needed by any tool. Connections without `scrape:read` must reconnect and approve it to run the scraping and search tools; `status` still uses `account:read`.

API keys remain supported for clients without OAuth and carry full account authority, so no scope is enforced against them. Authentication stays at the transport layer; tools never accept credentials as arguments.

## Run the MCP server locally

...

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TRANSPORT` | `stdio` | Selects `stdio` or `http`. |
| `HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | HTTP bind address; the Docker image uses `0.0.0.0`. |
| `PORT` | `8000` | HTTP listen port. |
| `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY` | — | Primary stdio credential. |
| `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` | — | Alternative stdio credential, also used by the Python SDK. |
| `MRSCRAPER_HTTP_AUTH` | `1` | Enables HTTP bearer verification. |
| `MRSCRAPER_OAUTH` | `1` | Accepts OAuth 2.1 access tokens alongside API keys. |
| `MRSCRAPER_MCP_PUBLIC_URL` | `https://mcp.mrscraper.com` | Public origin; `<origin>/mcp` is the required token audience. |
| `MRSCRAPER_OAUTH_ISSUER` | `https://api.app.mrscraper.com` | Authorization server issuer. |
| `MRSCRAPER_OAUTH_JWKS_URL` | `<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json` | Key set used to verify access tokens. |
| `MRSCRAPER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | — | Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the HTTP server. |
| `MRSCRAPER_API_BASE_URL` | MrScraper platform API | Platform endpoint override used by `status`. |
| `MRSCRAPER_FETCH_BASE_URL` | MrScraper Scraper API | Endpoint override used by the six scraping and search tools. |
| `MRSCRAPER_LOG_HTTP_PAYLOAD` | off | Enables ... |

...

|

## Security behavior

- HTTP authentication is enabled by default.
- Credential-bearing response headers are filtered from tool output.
- Credential metadata in scraping and search responses is redacted, and network errors redact signed query credentials.
- `status` preserves every field of the account status response body, including account identity and billing identifiers. Only credential-bearing response headers are removed.
- Browser-origin requests are accepted from trusted local origins, from `claude.ai` and `chatgpt.com`, and from exact values configured through `MRSCRAPER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.
- Tool calls receive the caller's authenticated OAuth token or API key through the MCP transport rather than through tool arguments.

auth.title: Authenticate Web Data Tools for AI Agents Without Exposing Secrets | MrScraper
highlights:
By MrScraper Team ·  October 15, 2026  · 10 min read

...

## Two ways to connect

Most teams use one of two patterns:

1. Your backend owns the key. Your server holds a MrScraper API token. The agent calls your tools, and your server calls MrScraper.
2. Each user connects their own account. A person signs in to MrScraper through their MCP client, such as Claude Code or Codex. The client handles the sign-in, and the agent uses that person's access. The next section covers when to use each one.

## When should you use API keys or OAuth?

| Use an API key when | Use OAuth when |
| --- | --- |
| Your app calls MrScraper on its own behalf | A person connects their own MrScraper account |
| The call runs on your server, a job runner or CI | The call runs from that person's MCP client |
| One account pays for and owns the usage | Each person's usage should stay on their account |
| You control where the key is stored | You do not want anyone to copy or paste a key |

### API keys for your backend

MrScraper API tokens are created in the dashboard under API Tokens. Each token has a name and an expiration date. You can create more than one, so you can give each environment or app its own token. See the API token docs for the steps.

The REST API reads the token from the `x-api-token` header. The Scraper API examples also pass it as a `token` query parameter. Your server sends both. The agent never sees either.

### OAuth for people using MCP clients

The hosted MrScraper MCP server at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` supports OAuth 2.1. The client opens a browser, the person signs in, and no key is copied anywhere.

To add it in Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp

```

To add it in Codex:

```bash
codex mcp add mrscraper --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp

```

OAuth access uses scopes:

- `scrape:read` covers the `scraperAPI` and `webSearch` tools.
- `account:read` covers the `status` tool. If a client calls a tool without the right scope, the server refuses it with a 403 `insufficient_scope` error. Grant only the scopes a person needs.

### When a client does not support OAuth

Some MCP clients cannot do the browser sign-in. For those, the MCP server accepts an API key as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. If you run it locally over stdio, it reads the key from the `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY` environment variable.

Point the client at the variable name, not the value, when it lets you. Codex supports this with a flag:

```bash
codex mcp add mrscraper --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var MRSCRAPER_API_KEY

```

If a client config file must hold the key, keep that file out of version control and readable only by you.

## Where should credentials live?

Keep credentials on the server, in one place, loaded once.

### Safe places

- An environment variable on your server
- Your cloud provider's secrets manager
- Your CI system's secret store, for batch jobs

### Unsafe places

- System prompts, user messages or tool results
- Tool input schemas, where the model would fill in the key
- Browser code, including front-end environment variables that get bundled into the page
- Your git repository
- Logs, error messages and analytics events MrScraper's docs say the same thing: never expose your API token in client-side code.

### Load the key once and keep it out of tool inputs

Read the key when the server starts. If it is missing, fail right away. Your tool functions use it directly, so it never appears in a tool schema or in anything the model sends.

```python
import os
import requests
 
MRSCRAPER_URL = "https://api.mrscraper.com/"
TOKEN = os.environ.get("MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN")
if not TOKEN:
    raise RuntimeError("MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN is not set")
 
 
def fetch_markdown(url: str) -> dict:
    response = requests.post(
        MRSCRAPER_URL,
        params={"token": TOKEN, "markdown": "true"},
        headers={"x-api-token": TOKEN, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
        json={"url": url, "maxRetries": 2},
        timeout=330,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

```

Notice that `fetch_markdown` takes only a URL. There is no `api_key` argument for the model to fill in.

### Scrub secrets from anything that leaves the server

Because the Scraper API examples put the token in the URL, a raw request URL can contain your key. Error messages from HTTP libraries often include that URL. So scrub every string before it goes to the model, a log or the browser.

```python
import re
 
 
def scrub(text: str) -> str:
    text = text.replace(TOKEN, "[REDACTED]")
    return re.sub(r"([?&]token=)[^&\s]+", r"\1[REDACTED]", text)
 
 
def safe_error(error: Exception) -> str:
    return scrub(str(error))

```

Use `safe_error` whenever you turn an exception into a tool result or a log line. Also check that your web server, load balancer and monitoring tools do not log full query strings for these requests.

### Put a tool gateway between the browser and the API

If your agent runs in a web app, the browser should talk to your server, never to MrScraper. Your server checks who the user is, then runs the tool.

```text
Browser  ->  Your server (checks user, runs tool)  ->  MrScraper API
            holds MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN

```

The browser sends its own session cookie or token to your server. Your server holds the MrScraper token. These are two different credentials, and that difference is the key to the next section.

## How do you separate user and service access?

There are two kinds of access in an agent app:

- User access answers "who is asking?" Your app's own login handles this.
- Service access answers "what is allowed to call MrScraper?" Your server's MrScraper token handles this. Never pass the service token to a user, and never let a user's request choose which token to use.

### Decide what each user can do

Your app should decide which tools each user can run and how much they can use. MrScraper sees one token. Your app knows which person is behind each call.

...

### Use separate tokens for separate jobs

Create one MrScraper token for each environment and each app. For example:

- `prod-research-agent`
- `staging-research-agent`
- `nightly-batch-jobs` This gives you three benefits. A leak in staging does not affect production. Each token's name shows up in your audit log. And you can replace one token without touching the others.

Set an expiration date on each token, and plan the swap before it expires. Create the new token, deploy it, check that calls succeed, and then retire the old one.

### When users bring their own accounts

Sometimes each user should use their own MrScraper account. In that case, skip the shared service token. Have each person connect through the hosted MCP server with OAuth. Their usage stays on their account, and the scopes limit what the client can do.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about plans, billing, and getting started with MrScraper.

  What do I get on the Scraper Free plan?   

 Scraper Free includes 1,000 MrScraper tokens every month at no cost - no credit card required. It's the fastest way to try scraping, proxies and AI extraction before upgrading. 

  Can I change plans later?   

 Yes. Upgrade from Scraper Free to Scraper Essential anytime from your account's billing settings for $99/month and 200,000 tokens, or move to a Custom plan by booking a call. 

  How do I get my API Token?   

 Sign in to the dashboard, open your account settings, and copy the token from the API Token page. Every API request authenticates with it, and the getting-started guide in the docs walks through your first call. 

  Can I use MrScraper without coding?   

 Yes. The visual scraper and AI Mode let you point at a page, describe the data you want, and get structured results without writing code. The API and SDKs are there when you want to automate further.

...

Does MrScraper provide built-in proxies?   

 Yes. Residential proxies with country-level targeting are built into the platform - enable them per scraper, with no third-party setup. Bandwidth is billed separately from plan tokens, from $1.5/GB.

...

How can I lower my scraping costs?   

 Tokens are charged on the data a scrape extracts, so collect only the fields you need, prefer Manual Mode for stable high-volume jobs, and schedule runs at the frequency the data actually changes.

...

My scheduled scrapes didn’t run - what can I check?   

 Check that the schedule is still enabled, your token balance isn't exhausted (extra usage is $1 per 1,000 tokens), and the target page still matches the scraper's setup. The run history shows each attempt's result - if it still looks wrong, contact support from the dashboard.

Compare MrScraper subscription plans, understand how token usage and billing cycles work, and choose the right plan for your scraping workload.

MrScraper offers flexible subscription plans designed for different usage levels, from individual developers testing the platform to enterprise teams running large-scale scraping operations. All plans include access to our AI-powered scraping agents, browser rendering, and residential proxies (on applicable plans).

## Available Plans

| Feature | Scraper Free | Scraper Pro | Scraper Enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API Tokens | 1,000 token | 200,000 token | Custom |
| Concurrent Requests | 10 | 100 | Custom |
| Residential Proxies | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Priority Email Support | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Dedicated Account Manager | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |

Free Plan Limitations

The Free plan includes 100 tokens per month with no credit card required. Tokens reset at the beginning of each month. Once your allocation is exhausted, you'll need to upgrade to continue scraping.

## Transaction Page

You can view your past transactions, by going to Account → Subscription. The transaction page displays a list of all your billing activities, including:

- Product
- Amount (Price)
- Status
- Date
- Invoice and Receipt links

...

To access the invoices or receipts of your account:

...

## Billing Cycle

### How Token Allocation Works

Monthly Plans:

- Tokens reset on your monthly renewal date
- Full token allotment available at the start of each cycle
- Unused tokens do not roll over to the next month

Annual Plans:

- Billed once per year
- Tokens still reset monthly on your renewal date
- 20% discount on total cost
- Unused tokens do not roll over

### Example Timeline

If you subscribe to Scraper Pro on January 15th:

| Date | Event | Token Balance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jan 15 | Subscription starts | 200,000 tokens |
| Jan 31 | Used 60,000 tokens | 140,000 tokens |
| Feb 15 | Billing cycle renews | 200,000 tokens (reset) |

Important

Unused tokens from the previous month are lost when your billing cycle renews. Plan your scraping operations accordingly to maximize your token allocation.

Monitor your token consumption and billing information through multiple channels:

- Dashboard: View real-time usage in your account API token dashboard
- API Endpoints: Track usage programmatically using our Analytics API

highlights:
# Workflow API Access

Learn how to run any scraper you have created through a MrScraper API endpoint, so you can automate scraping or integrate it into your application.

MrScraper lets you run any scraper you've created directly through an API endpoint. This is useful when you want to automate scraping, integrate it into your application, or test requests in tools like Postman.

## How to Run a Scraper Through the API

### Setup Steps

Open your dashboard and select a scraper you've already created. If you don't have one yet, create it first.

In the scraper window, click Settings.

Select AI Scraper API Access and slide to activate it.

Note

This turns off the AI chat for this scraper and enables API mode.

After activation, copy the example API request shown on the page.

Paste the request into Postman (or another API tool).

Note

You can replace the URL with any URL you want to scrape.

You can also run the scraper directly from Rerun an AI Scraper endpoint.

## API Request Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Location | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-api-token` | string | header | Yes | - | Your MrScraper API token |
| `scraperId` | string | body | Yes | - | The unique ID of the scraper you activated |
| `url` | string | body | Yes | - | The webpage URL you want to scrape |
| `maxRetry` | integer | body | No | `3` | Number of retry attempts if the scraping fails |
| `maxPages` | integer | body | No | 0 | Maximum number of pages to scrape (useful for listing/pagination). Use this to control how many pages you want to extract from multi-page listings |
| `timeout` | integer | body | No | `None` | Request timeout in seconds. Increase this value if you're scraping many pages or complex websites |
| `stream` | boolean | body | No | `false` | Enable streaming response mode. Highly recommended when scraping multiple pages that may take several minutes. If the connection is interrupted mid-process, you'll still receive the partial data that was already scraped from completed pages |

About maxPages

If the website has fewer pages than maxPages, it will scrape all available pages.

gate.title: Token Plan | MrScraper Documentation
highlights:
# Token Plan

Learn how plan tokens and API tokens work in MrScraper, why token usage varies between runs, and how to create your own API token for authentication.

MrScraper uses a token-based system for both usage and authentication.

- Plan Tokens measure how much you can use MrScraper's features, such as running or rerunning scrapers.
- API Tokens allow you to securely access the MrScraper API, for example, to rerun an existing scraper programmatically.

## Why Token Usage Varies

Token consumption isn't fixed — a few key factors affect how many tokens any given scraper uses:

- Website Complexity: Heavy JavaScript, dynamic content, or multiple requests increase runtime and token usage.
- Page Size and Content Density: Larger pages with long articles or extensive metadata produce more input text for AI models to process.
- Data Volume: Extracting large datasets (e.g., paginated listings) requires more compute and bandwidth.
- AI Processing Load: Complex instructions or large expected outputs increase input and output token usage.

Keep these in mind as you read the pricing tables below — they explain why two runs on the same plan can consume different amounts of tokens.

## Understanding Plan Tokens

Each MrScraper billing plan includes a specific number of tokens. Tokens represent the compute resources your scraper consumes — similar to how minutes or data are counted in a phone plan.

The number of tokens used depends on the type of scraper you run.

### AI Scraper Token Usage

AI Scrapers consume more tokens due to AI processing and additional factors such as:

| Usage Type | Description | Conversion Rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run Tracking | Each AI agent run consumes 5 tokens for trace tracking. Reruns and workflows consume 0 tokens for this component. | 0 or 5 tokens per run |
| Runtime | Time spent processing your task. | 1 token per 30 seconds of runtime |
| Input Tokens | Amount of text data (prompts or instructions) sent to the AI model. | 1 token per ~1,000 input tokens |
| Output Tokens | Amount of text generated by the AI model (responses or extracted results). | 1 token per ~200 output tokens |

...

| --- | --- | --- |

...

| 1 token per 30 seconds |

...

| 1 token per 0.25 MB |

...

### Scraper API Token Cap

The Scraper API token cap limits how many tokens a single scrape can use in the Scraper API. It applies only to Workflow and Scrape HTML, using the same runtime and bandwidth calculations shown in Workflow and Scrape HTML Token Usage.

When Retry is enabled, a failed scrape retries automatically. Two limits control how far retrying goes:

- Max retries: The maximum number of retry attempts (3 by default).
- Token cap: The maximum total tokens all attempts can use (Unlimited by default).

Retrying stops at the first of these: the scrape succeeds, it reaches Max retries, or the running token total reaches the token cap. Each attempt's token cost is rounded up (ceiling rule) and added to a running total.

The token cap takes effect only when Retry is enabled, since its purpose is to limit how many tokens retries can consume. If Retry is off, the scrape runs once and returns a result or an error.

...

### Marketplace Scraper Token Usage

Marketplace Scrapers use a custom token cost based on factors such as the target domain, workflow complexity, proxy usage, infrastructure requirements, and scraper configuration. Each scraper may use either a fixed token cost or a custom usage calculation depending on how the scraper is designed.

For the complete list of Marketplace Scraper token costs, see the Marketplace catalog.

# Create and Run a Scraper Programmatically

Learn how to create an AI scraper once in the dashboard and then run it programmatically through the API. Set up once, automate everywhere.

## Overview

This guide shows you how to create an AI scraper in the dashboard and then use it programmatically through the API. This is perfect if you want to set up a scraper once and automate data extraction with simple API calls—no need to configure it every time.

## Prerequisites

Before you start, make sure you have:

- A MrScraper API token for authentication. If you don’t have one yet, follow this guide to create an API token.

## Verify Your API Token

You can verify your API token and check your account status using the `/subscription-accounts`:

cURL JavaScript Python

Copy Text

```
curl --location 'https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts' \
--header 'accept: */*' \
--header 'x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>'
```

...

Key Response Fields:

Subscription Account Fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Unique identifier for your subscription account |
| `tokenLimit` | integer | Maximum tokens available in your subscription plan |
| `tokenUsage` | integer | Total tokens consumed so far |
| `stripeSubscriptionId` | string | Stripe subscription identifier (for billing) |
| `userId` | string | Your unique user identifier |
| `stripeStatus` | string | Payment status (`"true"` = active) |
| `quantity` | integer | Subscription quantity/seats |
| `endsAt` | string | Subscription expiration date (ISO 8601 format) |
| `subscriptionItemId` | string | Stripe subscription item identifier |
| `rateLimit` | integer/null | API rate limit (requests per window) |
| `rateTtl` | integer/null | Rate limit time window in seconds |
| `isEnterprise` | boolean | Whether account has enterprise features |
| `cancelAtPeriodEnd` | boolean/null | If subscription will cancel at period end |
| `currentPeriodStart` | string/null | Current billing period start date |
| `currentPeriodEnd` | string/null | Current billing period end date |
| `proxyDollarPerGB` | number/null | Custom proxy pricing (enterprise only) |
| `isAutoRenew` | boolean | Whether subscription auto-renews |

...

Tip

Checking Token Balance: Use `tokenLimit - tokenUsage` to calculate your remaining tokens. Plan your scraping operations accordingly to avoid running out of tokens.

highlights:
# MCP Server

Official MrScraper MCP server for retrieving web pages, web search, and account usage. Connect AI clients or run the open-source server locally.

MrScraper MCP is the official Model Context Protocol server for MrScraper. It connects AI clients to web page retrieval, web search, and your account usage.

MrScraper MCP server source code on GitHub · Install the @mrscraper/mcp npm package

The server exposes seven tools:

### status

Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields.

### scrapeHtml

Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional.

### scrapeMarkdown

Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON.

### getScreenshot

Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled.

### scrapeBrand

Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON.

### scrapeJson

Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output.

### webSearch

Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources.

Use the hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint for a managed connection, or run the published MCP package locally through Streamable HTTP or stdio.

Package information

This page documents `@mrscraper/mcp` version 0.5.0. Its seven tools share their descriptions, inputs, and defaults with the MrScraper CLI, SDKs, and integrations. 0.5.0 replaced `scraperAPI` with `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, and `getScreenshot`, added `scrapeBrand` and `scrapeJson`, renamed the inputs to camel case, and changed the OAuth scopes. See Migration from the previous tool set.

## Capabilities

### Page Retrieval

Retrieve a known URL as HTML, Markdown, or a screenshot, with optional browser rendering, real-device routing, proxy controls, selector waiting, and retry limits.

### Brand and JSON Extraction

Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links, or structured JSON from a natural-language prompt.

### Web Search

Search the web for ranked results, for a chosen country and up to 100 results at a time.

### Account Status

Read the subscription, token limit, token usage, remaining tokens, and rate limit.

### Managed Endpoint

Connect to the hosted MCP endpoint through Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in.

### Structured Tool Results

Receive a consistent response envelope in MCP structured content.

### Interactive Widgets

Render search results and an account usage meter in hosts that support MCP Apps.

## Requirements

- A MrScraper account
- An MCP client with Streamable HTTP support
- An API key only when the client cannot use OAuth 2.1 or when running the server locally

## Quick start with the hosted server

Add the hosted endpoint

Configure a Streamable HTTP server named `mrscraper` with no credential:

Copy Text

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Use this exact URL, including the `/mcp` path.

Sign in

Connect or reload the MCP server. Your client follows the OAuth 2.1 challenge, opens MrScraper in your browser, and asks you to approve `scrape:read` for the six scraping and search tools and `account:read` for `status`.

Reload and verify

Reload the client or start a new session, then inspect its MCP tool list. The connection should expose `status`, `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, `getScreenshot`, `scrapeBrand`, `scrapeJson`, and `webSearch`.

...

Add the hosted URL without a static `Authorization` header, then complete browser sign-in when the client prompts you.

...

```

...

## API key fallback

If a client cannot complete OAuth, create an API key, store it through the client's secret mechanism, and send it as a bearer token:

Copy Text

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

For Codex, pass the environment-variable name instead of embedding the key:

Copy Text

```
export MRSCRAPER_API_KEY="YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
codex mcp add mrscraper \
  --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var MRSCRAPER_API_KEY
```

## Authentication

| Connection | Credential source |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted Streamable HTTP | OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in, or an API key fallback |
| Self-hosted Streamable HTTP | OAuth 2.1 access token, or `Authorization: Bearer <MrScraper API key>` |
| Local stdio | `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY`, then `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` |

The hosted server publishes OAuth 2.1 protected-resource metadata and challenges unauthenticated clients to start browser sign-in. Access tokens are issued for the exact `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` resource. A tool called without its required scope returns `403 insufficient_scope`, and your client can offer to grant the missing permission.

| Scope | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| `scrape:read` | `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, `getScreenshot`, `scrapeBrand`, `scrapeJson`, and `webSearch` |
| `account:read` | `status` |

These are the only application scopes the server advertises; the authorization server also offers `offline_access` for refresh tokens. Clients take the scopes from the server's metadata, so don't pin scopes in client configurations.

OAuth connections that already hold `scrape:read` keep working without reconnecting; `scrape:write` is no longer needed by any tool. Connections without `scrape:read` must reconnect and approve it to run the scraping and search tools; `status` still uses `account:read`.

API keys remain supported for clients without OAuth and carry full account authority, so no scope is enforced against them. Authentication stays at the transport layer; tools never accept credentials as arguments.

## Run the MCP server locally

Node.js 20 or newer is required.

### Published package over stdio

Copy Text

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@mrscraper/mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "MRSCRAPER_API_KEY": "YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Source checkout over Streamable HTTP

Clone and build

Copy Text

```
git clone https://github.com/mrscraper-com/mrscraper-mcp.git
cd mrscraper-mcp
npm ci
npm run build
```

Start HTTP transport

Copy Text

```
TRANSPORT=http npm start
```

The default endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`.

Connect the client

Copy Text

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mrscraper": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

...

## Security behavior

- HTTP authentication is enabled by default.
- Credential-bearing response headers are filtered from tool output.
- Credential metadata in scraping and search responses is redacted, and network errors redact signed query credentials.
- `status` preserves every field of the account status response body, including account identity and billing identifiers. Only credential-bearing response headers are removed.
- Browser-origin requests are accepted from trusted local origins, from `claude.ai` and `chatgpt.com`, and from exact values configured through `MRSCRAPER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.
- Tool calls receive the caller's authenticated OAuth token or API key through the MCP transport rather than through tool arguments.

## Choosing the right tool

| Starting point | Desired outcome | Tool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A known URL | Raw HTML | `scrapeHtml` |
| A known URL | Markdown, or Markdown and HTML together | `scrapeMarkdown` |
| A known URL | A screenshot of the full page or top viewport | `getScreenshot` |
| A website | Colors, typography, logos, and social links | `scrapeBrand` |
| A known URL | Data extracted as JSON with a natural-language prompt | `scrapeJson` |
| A topic or keyword | Search result discovery | `webSearch` |
| An account | Plan, token usage, and remaining tokens | `status` |

A discovery workflow commonly uses `webSearch` first, followed by `scrapeMarkdown` or `scrapeHtml` for the pages that will inform the answer. Agents produce summaries, tables, and structured output from the retrieved content, or call `scrapeJson` to have MrScraper extract the data.

### Migration from the previous tool set

Version 0.5.0 replaces the tools and inputs of version 0.4:

| Previous | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `scraperAPI` | `scrapeHtml` for raw HTML, `scrapeMarkdown` for Markdown (with `html: true`, Markdown and HTML), or `getScreenshot` for a screenshot. Brand and JSON extraction are the separate `scrapeBrand` and `scrapeJson` tools. |
| `scraperAPI` inputs `geo_code`, `proxy_country`, `browser_rendering`, `wait_for_selector`, `block_resources`, `max_retries`, and `home_page` | `geoCode`, `proxyCountry`, `browserRendering`, `waitForSelector`, `blockResources`, `maxRetries`, and `warmStart`. |
| `scraperAPI` inputs `use_proxy`, `bypass_proxy`, `cookie_jar`, `headers`, `token_cap`, `stream`, and `discard_token_secret` | Removed. |
| `webSearch` inputs `url`, `region`, `num_results`, and `timeout` | `query`, `country`, and `numResults`. `query` is search text; a search results URL is no longer read for its `q` parameter. The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. |
| `status` summary fields, such as `token_remaining` and `usage_percent` | The raw account status body, with account details at `data.data`. |
| OAuth scopes `scrape:read` and `scrape:write` | `scrape:read` for all six scraping and search tools; `scrape:write` is no longer needed. `status` still uses `account:read`. |

Browser rendering no longer switches on automatically. It is off unless `browserRendering` is true; `getScreenshot` always renders, and `scrapeMarkdown` renders when `html` is true. The page timeout defaults to 300 seconds (was 120), and omitting `maxRetries` means no retry limit (was 3). ChatGPT and Codex sign-ins, which got a reduced `scraperAPI` in 0.4, now receive the same seven tools and inputs as every other client.

Start a new client session or reconnect so the client refreshes its tool list.

...

## Common response envelope

Every tool returns the same envelope in MCP `structuredContent` and as formatted JSON in a text content block:

Copy Text

```
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "[Formatted JSON matching structuredContent]"
    }
  ],
  "structuredContent": {
    "status_code": 200,
    "data": "<html><body>Example page content...</body></html>",
    "headers": {
      "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status_code` | number or `null` | HTTP status returned by the MrScraper service, or `null` when the request ends before an HTTP response arrives. |
| `data` | JSON value, string, or `null` | The API response body, as parsed JSON or text. Its field names are not converted. |
| `headers` | object | Response headers with credential-bearing headers filtered out. |
| `error` | string, when present | Request failure summary. |

`status` preserves the complete account status body without adding summary fields.

### Error handling

HTTP and network failures set `isError: true` on the MCP tool result and include `error` in the envelope. Network failures use `status_code: null`. Invalid inputs, including inputs a tool does not define, are rejected before any upstream call. Authentication and missing OAuth scopes are enforced by the HTTP transport before a tool runs.

## Tool reference

Tool names, descriptions, inputs, and defaults match the MrScraper CLI, SDKs, and integrations. Inputs use camel case and are sent to the API under the same names. Tools authenticate through the MCP connection and do not accept a token argument.

| Tool | Title | OAuth scope | `readOnlyHint` | `openWorldHint` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | Account Status | `account:read` | `true` | `false` |
| `scrapeHtml` | Scrape HTML | `scrape:read` | `false` | `true` |
| `scrapeMarkdown` | Scrape Markdown | `scrape:read` | `false` | `true` |
| `getScreenshot` | Get Screenshot | `scrape:read` | `false` | `true` |
| `scrapeBrand` | Scrape Brand | `scrape:read` | `true` | `true` |
| `scrapeJson` | Scrape JSON | `scrape:read` | `false` | `true` |
| `webSearch` | Web Search | `scrape:read` | `true` | `true` |

Every tool sets `destructiveHint: false`. `scrapeHtml`, `scrapeMarkdown`, `getScreenshot`, and `scrapeJson` are not marked read-only because `saveResult` can save their results to your dashboard. The six scraping and search tools use tokens from your plan.

Examples use `https://example.com` as the sample target. Replace it for your use case. Response examples show the envelope from `structuredContent`, with selected keys and types observed in live API responses. Values are placeholders; page content, base64 images, and arrays are abbreviated. Actual responses may contain additional fields.

### Shared parameters

HTML, Markdown, screenshots, and JSON extraction share `url`, `timeout`, `geoCode`, `proxyCountry`, `super`, `waitUntil`, `proxy`, `maxRetries`, and `saveResult`. Page defaults are 300 seconds, US geolocation and proxy country, real-device routing off, and dashboard saving off. Omitted retry limits mean no limit.

HTML, Markdown, and screenshots additionally accept `blockResources`, `waitForSelector`, and `returnCookie`. JSON extraction does not accept these controls. Browser rendering is optional for HTML, Markdown, and JSON; screenshots always enable it. Markdown with HTML also enables browser rendering.

The six scraping and search tools send `GET` requests to the Scraper API with their inputs as query parameters:

Copy Text

```
GET https://api.mrscraper.com
```

Each tool's table lists its complete inputs.

...

### `scrapeHtml`

Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional.

...

### `webSearch`

Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | Required | Search query text, trimmed before sending, containing 1 to 1000 characters. |
| `country` | string | `"us"` | Two-letter country code to search from, sent in lowercase. |
| `numResults` | integer | `10` | Number of search results to request, as an integer from 10 to 100. Fewer results may be returned. |

The HTTP deadline is fixed at 120 seconds. It is not a service parameter.
